The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks!D42 asks for binary pass/fail behavior and anchored Likert craft; Internal Quality Checks!E42 contains the historical binary-plus-weight note. All Functional descriptions were read: they demand discrete validation, arithmetic, permission, mutation, lineage, record fidelity, concurrency or durability outcomes, not degrees of craft. Polish judge.toml:20-59 tests retained inputs, real refusal, successful correction/retry and same-operation continuity; its prompt.md:10 explicitly says to assess real stateful recovery, not visual craft. These are observable pass/fail outcomes despite the Polish dimension name. Visual judge.toml:20-29,35-44,50-59,65-74,80-89 gives every typography, palette, layout, hierarchy and component-consistency criterion type=likert, points=5 and distinct anchors 5,4,3,2,1. The intermediate anchors describe minor, noticeable and substantial defects; none merely repeats a yes/no requirement. Visual prompt.md:8 requests those five anchors and uses raw 1 as normalized zero for an observed failed gate; line 10 permits alternate layouts/labels/styles and excludes screenshot, phone-layout and theme demands. TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md:160 explains the corrected 1-5 scale despite the starter template extra raw-0 anchors. This corroborates scale compatibility, not aesthetic judgment.
